# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.21 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.20. Written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64.**

**New / fixed**
- **Cut line on sheets turned by 90° or 270°.** A cut line dragged on the original (or `--cut-at`) now works at every rotation. On a sheet turned by a quarter the line becomes horizontal and the two pages come out one above the other, the page that was on the left of the original first. Tested on synthetic sheets (sizes and page order); not tried in the window.
- **File dialogs that cannot open.** When the system has no file-dialog provider, a click on "Add images…", "Open/Save project…" or "Export PDF…" used to do nothing at all. The window now says so (in all 8 interface languages) and points to dragging files in or the command line. A dialog that closes within 0.4 s is taken as "none available", so a very fast Cancel on a slow machine can show the message too.

**Tried in a real window on Linux (checks, not changes)**: the native file dialogs (GTK dialog through an xdg desktop portal): "Export PDF…" wrote a 6-page PDF, "Save project…" and "Open project…" round-tripped. Windows and macOS dialogs: not tried.

**Known limits (unchanged)**: OCR can misread characters such as `@` (see the `--redact` warnings added in pre.20); the rotation behaviour seen on Windows 11 is unconfirmed; the sideways check was validated on about 100 pages only; Windows, macOS and arm64 builds are untested by the author.
